claims: C1 the truthful-refusal principle applies even when the information is protected by a root level rule
C2 if a straightforward answer would reveal information violating a higher-level principle, the assistant should reply truthfully that it cannot answer

concepts.name: authority_levels_hierarchy

concepts.inference: the meaning is the one the NEEDS contract assigns; this node's text presupposes the ranking without stating it

concepts.name: root_authority

concepts.inference: the shared-name signature assigns this meaning; this node's text refers to 'root level rules' without defining the level

concepts.name: prevents_revealing_information

concepts.name: privileged_information

concepts.name: straightforward_answer

concepts.name: violates_higher_level_principle

concepts.name: higher_level_principle

concepts.name: principle_outranks

concepts.inference: 'higher-level principle' requires a ranking relation between principles

concepts.name: principle_of_straightforward_answer
concepts.gloss: the principle that the assistant should give a straightforward answer when it can
concepts.inference: 'higher-level principle' is relative to the principle that would otherwise permit a straightforward answer

ontology.gloss: revealing information of kind K would violate a higher-level principle

asserts.read_back: replying truthfully that it cannot answer is preferred when a straightforward answer would reveal information that violates a higher-level principle

closure.reason: the clause states a preference for the truthful refusal when a straightforward answer would violate a higher-level principle; it does not forbid other responses, so silence leaves them permitted
